title: ContraDB's ¶
assumes: The last call of the pass is the one that carries it: the neighbour swing at the end of B2, once for the ones' pass and once for the twos'.
quotes: ContraDB: “8: neighbors swing ⁋” — the last figure of B2, in both halves of the dance.
notes: ContraDB marks the figure that carries the progression with a pilcrow, and Jeremy Corners has one per pass, on B2's neighbour swing. It is the last call of the pass, so this reading puts the shift a beat earlier than the engine's own pass boundary — and the difference is the mechanism, because a call that carries the progression at its end slides the dancers it leaves out along with their own line (M9g) and a boundary does not. **Measured** at six couples: `closure 23.0000 · progressed 37.7359 · reach 25.5545 short · collision 0.000`, against the record's `0.0000 · 37.7359 · 0.0000 · 0.000`. It moves `progressed` not at all and costs the most reach of the four readings — the B2 swing is a gatherer, and the slide the clause gives the dancers it leaves out pulls the ring apart under it. Taking the shift at the swing's **start** instead was measured and **not taken**: at six couples it reads `closure 32.0000 · progressed 32.0000 · reach 5.4301 short · collision 0.000` — better on `progressed` and on reach, worse on nothing. It is not taken because a pilcrow marks the figure that carries the progression and `"progresses": true` is what “this call carries it” means; `"start"` is a second reading of ContraDB's mark rather than the same one, and inventing it to improve a number is oracle-tuning. If the user picks this column, that is the next question to put to them.
